Subject: HydraHealth: procurement portal requirements and PO export format

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking this on. We're preparing Redwood for Ariba supplier enrollment and want to confirm a few things before we kick off:

- Vendor registration: HydraHealth requires supplier to register via Ariba Supplier Network (link below). We'll need the Dun & Bradstreet number in the profile and a primary contact.
- PO export: our ERP expects a CSV extract with these fields: PONumber, PODate (ISO), LineNo, SKU, QtyOrdered, UnitPrice, NetAmount, TaxAmount, Currency, BuyerCode, DeliveryAddressCode. (Attached: Hydra_PO_spec.csv)
- EDI vs. PDF: we prefer EDI-850, but can accept CSV exports if EDI is not feasible within the first month.
- Order of execution: vendor registration -> MSA & order form signed -> PO issuance. We can provision sandbox POs as soon as vendor shows registered status.

Two asks from our side: can Redwood provide an Order Form backfill that maps Redwood product SKUs to Hydra SKU codes, and can legal confirm whether your standard payment terms (Net30) are editable on the order form export?

Link to supplier registration: https://supplier.ariba.com/registration/HYDRA-5521
Attachment: Hydra_PO_spec.csv (CSV, 6KB)

Thanks — looking to get this live before year-end.

—ProcureOps
Procurement Operations
HydraHealth

ProcureOps —

Appreciate the detail. Quick notes:

- For the PO export, our engineering team can map Redwood SKUs to your SKU codes. I'll attach a draft order form with mapping placeholders (orderform_redline_v1.pdf). Can you have your ERP team verify the column order?
- Regarding EDI — we support EDI in Dedicated integrations but not for Hosted on Day 1. If EDI is required immediately, we'll need Ben and Lauren to scope the work. Otherwise we'll provide the CSV export and a PDF copy for EDI-compatibility checks.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm DUNS & remit address (ProcureOps)

Looping in Ben (legal) and Lauren (operations) to confirm the order-form redlines and whether Net30 will be modifiable per-order.

Thanks,

Karthik / ProcureOps —

I've reviewed the MSA and the draft order form. High level summary of redlines attached (OrderForm_MSA_redlines.docx):

- Payment terms: Redwood standard is Net30; if Hydra needs earlier payment dates (Net15) that's a negotiable point but will affect pricing.
- Data handling: we accept standard audit logs but will not agree to data-persistence beyond our retention policy unless there's a compensated addendum.
- Liability cap: propose $5M or 2x fees (whichever is greater). Hydra's clause was unlimited for consequential damages; that's a hard stop.
- PO acceptance: suggest adding a 5-business-day automatic acceptance window on electronic PO to avoid manual acknowledgments blocking fulfillment.

Ben's asks for ProcureOps: please confirm whether Hydra will accept DocuSign for the order form (we prefer that) and if you require countersignature in Ariba itself. Also please confirm the DUNS number so we can populate the supplier profile.

Attachment: OrderForm_MSA_redlines.docx (14KB)

—Ben Carter
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference

Ben / Karthik —

Thanks for the redlines. Quick answers:

- DocuSign: yes, we can accept DocuSign for the order form; signature in Ariba is optional but we can record the DocuSign envelope in Ariba. We'll send DocuSign instructions once the final document is provided.
- DUNS: Hydra DUNS for this buyer unit is 55-123-987. Please include it in the supplier profile.
- Ariba registration: we've added Redwood to our supplier list. Supplier ID HYD-RED-0098. Once you complete the registration page we can move to sandbox POs.
- PO export note: their CSV sample looks good; our ERP team asked that currency be explicit (USD) and that address codes match the deliver-to codes in the attachment. See attached screenshot of the Ariba supplier summary for reference.

Attachment: ariba_screenshot.png (PNG, 120KB)

I'll ask procurement to create a DocuSign envelope after you resend the redlined order form as a Word/PDF doc.
